key_insight: Equilibrated flux estimators can give a guaranteed, computable upper bound on finite element error even on coarse or badly distorted meshes, without relying on shape-regularity assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers quantify simulation reliability for real-world geometries and poor-quality meshes, where classical a posteriori theory may not apply.
method: Use an equilibrated flux estimator to bound the energy-norm discretization error.
Avoid shape-regularity, quasi-uniformity, and angle-condition assumptions in the reliability proof.
Rely only on a cell-level Poincaré constant, with Payne–Weinberger giving a bound of at most hK/π for convex cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract argues analytically that the estimator remains fully computable and guaranteed with constant one, with distortion affecting only efficiency rather than reliability.
watch_item: Very distorted meshes may make the estimator pessimistic, so the bound can be safe but not sharp.
paper_title: A posteriori error estimation for coarse or distorted meshes
